rows.headline: Australia introduces legislation for a domestic gas reservation scheme for LNG exporters
rows.hook: Canberra mandates domestic supply for LNG exporters
rows.summary: The Australian government will introduce a bill next week requiring LNG exporters to reserve up to 20 percent of total production for the domestic market. The scheme aims to address expected east coast supply shortages by the end of the decade and will officially take effect on July 1, 2027. Major gas producers have raised concerns that the mandate could undermine Australia's standing as a reliable global LNG supplier. Indian energy companies relying on Australian LNG imports could face shifting supply dynamics.
rows.whats_next: Bill introduction in the Australian parliament next week
rows.why_it_matters: Potential shifts in long-term LNG import costs for Indian buyers
rows.winners_losers: Domestic Australian gas users gain / LNG exporters hurt

rows.headline: Nvidia changes its method for calculating cash flow to balance buybacks and AI investments
rows.hook: New math for Nvidia's massive cash pile
rows.summary: Nvidia has quietly altered how it measures cash flow, signaling a strategic shift in balancing capital returns to shareholders with building out its artificial intelligence ecosystem. This accounting tweak could alter the scale and pacing of future share buybacks by the chip maker. While US-listed, Nvidia's decisions ripple through the global semiconductor supply chain and heavily influence tech-heavy sentiment in broader markets. Indian retail investors tracking global tech trends should note how capital allocation at the world's leading AI chip maker evolves.

rows.why_it_matters: Signals future pacing of Nvidia buybacks and global tech sentiment.
